title: Verify, Don't Opine: Why Manager Agents Make Reports Worse
summary: A Leiden experiment shows that letting a manager agent send work back made reports more hedged and 51.5% more expensive, with no quality gain, unless the manager can actually verify something. Plus: one prompt that unlocked every Bedrock agent in an AWS account, silicon samples tested like stated-preference surveys, and Epoch's 13x-a-year drop in the price of AI performance.
shownotes:
AgentCorruption: one chat message to a public Bedrock agent reached IMDS, stole STS credentials and unlocked every agent in the AWS account; scope your execution role, block link-local egress, treat memory as an attack surface.
Silicon samples tested like a stated-preference survey: newer models pass theory-based validity tests yet miss human willingness-to-pay by 4 to 6x; coherent is not correct.
Epoch AI: the price of a fixed level of AI performance falls about 13x a year (47% per quarter since 2023), faster than DNA sequencing, compute, batteries or electricity.
CrowdStrike: a likely single operator used the open-source agentic pentest tool ARTEX against South Korean banks, with 25,000+ records stolen at Shinhan Bank.
Deep dive: a LIACS Leiden paired experiment finds flat pipelines beat manager-with-loop-back on utility and clarity; the harm comes from the revision step, not the hierarchy. Tie revisions to verifier failures, not a manager's taste.
